intent: Hold the chosen value of a pick-one field and tie a trigger to the popup list of options it opens.
typical_uses: A form field choosing one value from a fixed list of options
A compact toolbar control narrowing a list by one attribute

dont_use_when.situation: A short list of choices that should all stay visible at once
A long list the user needs to search or filter by typing
A list of actions or commands rather than a value to keep
A field where the platform's own picker is wanted (the native mobile wheel, native autofill)

invariants.text: `value` and `defaultValue` are both accepted; `defaultValue` seeds the initial state and is ignored afterwards, and when `value` is given it wins and the component follows it on every render.
`open` and `defaultOpen` are both accepted; `defaultOpen` seeds the initial state and is ignored afterwards, and when `open` is given it wins and the component follows it on every render.

The SelectValue in the trigger resolves the selected item's caption from the root alone: from `itemToStringLabel`, from a value object carrying `label`, or from `items`; with none of them it shows the value itself converted to a string, never the text of the matching SelectItem.
Without `multiple`, choosing an item sets the value and closes the popup; with `multiple`, `value` is an array, choosing an item adds it or removes it, and the popup stays open.

Without `multiple`, typing while the closed trigger has focus selects the next enabled item whose text starts with the typed characters and reports it through `onValueChange`, without opening the popup.
The root renders a hidden input carrying the value as a string; with `name` it submits with the enclosing form, and under `multiple` one hidden input per chosen value carries the name instead.

While open and `modal` is not false, the select locks page scroll and lays a backdrop that blocks pointer interaction outside it; Escape or a press outside closes it and reports the change through `onOpenChange`.
`disabled` and `readOnly` both stop the trigger from opening the popup and stop any item from being chosen, even in a popup held open through `open` or `defaultOpen`.

anti_patterns.dont: Leave out `items` when the item values are identifiers rather than the captions a user reads
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass `items` as the same `{ value, label }` list the SelectItems are rendered from, so the closed trigger shows the caption

value.states: value is the chosen item's value, of the caller's own Value type, an array of them under `multiple`, or null for no choice
value.because: `SelectValueType<Value, Multiple> | null` - typed by the root's own generic parameters, which the caller chooses, so no JSON Schema type can state what it holds.

defaultValue.states: defaultValue is the initially chosen item's value, of the same type as `value`
defaultValue.because: Same generic type as `value` above - `SelectValueType<Value, Multiple> | null`, chosen by the caller.

onValueChange.states: onValueChange is a callback called with the next value and event details, not a value
onValueChange.because: `(value, eventDetails) => void` - a function of the root's own generic value type plus Base UI's change-event details, including the reason (an item press, typeahead on the closed trigger, ...). No JSON Schema type covers a function.

multiple.states: multiple switches the value to an array of chosen item values when true
multiple.because: Typed as the root's own `Multiple` type parameter, which also retypes `value`, `defaultValue` and `onValueChange`; the schema can state that it is a boolean, not that coupling.

items.states: items is the option data the root resolves the selected caption from - a value-to-label record, a list of `{ value, label }`, or a list of labelled groups of them
items.because: `Record<string, ReactNode> | { label: ReactNode; value: any }[] | Group[]` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property, and the labels are React nodes.

itemToStringLabel.states: itemToStringLabel is a function turning an item value into the caption the trigger shows
itemToStringLabel.because: `(itemValue: Value) => string` - a function, which no JSON Schema type covers. It is meant for object values without a `label`.

itemToStringValue.states: itemToStringValue is a function turning an item value into the string the hidden input submits
itemToStringValue.because: `(itemValue: Value) => string` - a function, which no JSON Schema type covers. It is meant for object values without a `value` field.

isItemEqualToValue.states: isItemEqualToValue is a function deciding whether an item's value matches the chosen value; without it the root compares with Object.is
isItemEqualToValue.because: `(itemValue: Value, value: Value) => boolean` - a function, which no JSON Schema type covers. It is meant for object values that are equal without being the same object.

onOpenChange.states: onOpenChange is a callback called with the next open state and event details, not a value
onOpenChange.because: `(open: boolean, eventDetails) => void`; the second argument carries Base UI's change-event details, including the reason (a trigger press, an item press, an outside press, Escape, ...). No JSON Schema type covers a function.

onOpenChangeComplete.states: onOpenChangeComplete is a callback called with the open state once the open or close animation has finished
onOpenChangeComplete.because: `(open: boolean) => void` - a function, which no JSON Schema type covers.

actionsRef.states: actionsRef is a ref the root fills with an imperative `unmount` action
actionsRef.because: `React.RefObject<SelectRootActions | null>` - a ref object holding a function, which no JSON Schema type covers.

inputRef.states: inputRef is a ref to the hidden input the root renders for form submission
inputRef.because: `React.Ref<HTMLInputElement>` is a union of a ref object and a callback function - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

children.states: children is the root's content, the parts listed under accepts
children.because: `React.ReactNode` is a union of elements, strings, numbers, fragments and more; the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

good.title: A controlled select with its caption data
An uncontrolled select submitted with a form
good.code:
<Select name="role" defaultValue="viewer" items={ROLES}>
  <SelectTrigger aria-label="Role">
    <SelectValue />
  </SelectTrigger>
  <SelectContent>
    <SelectItem value="viewer">Viewer</SelectItem>
    <SelectItem value="editor">Editor</SelectItem>
  </SelectContent>
</Select>

bad.title: A placeholder passed to the root
bad.code:
<Select placeholder="Pick a region" items={REGIONS}>
  <SelectTrigger aria-label="Region">
    <SelectValue />
  </SelectTrigger>
  <SelectContent>
    <SelectItem value="eu-central">Frankfurt</SelectItem>
  </SelectContent>
</Select>
bad.why: The root takes no placeholder; it belongs to SelectValue, which shows it while nothing is chosen.
